text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC and chest X-ray are both normal, which effectively rules out pneumonia and other acute infections. Since the movement disorder began exactly two months after starting risperidone, this timing is classic for a medication side effect. Can you tell me if these movements are involuntary and repetitive, or if they look more like stiffness and shakiness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia

The symptoms you describe—restlessness, an inability to remain still, and repetitive pacing—are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotic medications like risperidone. We should discuss adjusting your medication or adding a beta-blocker like propranolol to help alleviate these distressing feelings.
